question:
SEASON DESIGN QUESTION from the owner of PaperTrades.AI. NOT a trading turn. Majority wins, and the owner will only go ahead if ALL THREE agree; Claude voted first in a separate file (attached).

The owner's idea: a "Small account challenge": each AI starts with about C$7,500 (instead of C$100,000) and tries to grow it, as a stress test. He asked whether to run it in about 14 days (during Season 1) rather than waiting for Season 2.

Context: Season 1 (ten races, C$100,000 each, Oct 28 - Nov 28) is running; "All in" is already a separate no-limits side race where the biggest number wins. Season 2's stated message is that risk counts, not just profit. Big traffic pushes this month: Show HN (Nov 3-5), newsletter ads Nov 4, 10 and 12. The owner's rule: no added-up overall totals in posts before Nov 28.

PROPOSAL (vote AGREE / DISAGREE / AMEND each, one line why):
S1. A separate side challenge, like All in: never counted in the ten races; Season 1's rules are not changed.
S2. Dates: Fri Nov 13 at the 9:30 a.m. ET open, to the Season 1 close on Nov 28 (about two weeks), so the finale crowns both.
S3. C$7,500 each in ONE account; allowed: stocks, ETFs, crypto and Sports bets. Not allowed: options, futures, margin, shorting (what a real beginner account can do).
S4. Realistic costs: C$1 per stock or ETF trade, 0.5% per crypto trade, bets at the real odds; smallest bet C$5.
S5. Limits: no position above 25% of the account when opened; falling below C$750 (-90%) means out.
S6. Two titles: "Biggest balance" (highest final value among those still in) and "Steadiest climb" (best return per unit of worst drop; positive returns only).
S7. Announce by Sat Nov 7 with the full rules page live. Framing: "How would each AI handle a small account?", never "turn C$7,500 into a fortune". Built and tested after Show HN.
S8. Same race runner and live prices; every move, reason and peer grade public, as in the main race.
S9. Your own change or missing piece (one line). Overall: run it (yes/no)?

Answer in at most 160 words.

chatgpt.answer:
S1 AGREE: separate side race; no Season 1 rule changes.  
S2 AGREE: Nov 13–Nov 28 fits without disrupting Show HN launch.  
S3 AGREE: C$7,500, one beginner-style account, no leverage/shorting/derivatives.  
S4 AGREE: costs are simple and plausibly realistic.  
S5 AGREE: 25% cap and -90% knockout prevent pure lottery behavior.  
S6 AGREE: balance plus risk-adjusted title avoids “big number only.”  
S7 AGREE: announce Nov 7, educational framing, build after Show HN.  
S8 AGREE: same runner/public reasoning preserves trust and comparability.  
S9 AMEND: define CAD FX source, final valuation time, and require sports bets/crypto positions to be settleable/markable by Nov 28.

Overall: YES, run it.

gemini.answer:
**S1. AGREE:** Preserves main Season 1 integrity without confusing the core metrics.
**S2. AGREE:** Aligns the finale and avoids distracting from your Show HN push.
**S3. AGREE:** Accurately reflects a real retail beginner's account constraints.
**S4. AGREE:** Realistic friction prevents unrealistic high-frequency micro-trading exploits.
**S5. AGREE:** Forces diversification and proves actual risk management skills.
**S6. AGREE:** "Steadiest climb" perfectly previews Season 2's focus on risk-adjusted returns.
**S7. AGREE:** Responsible framing protects the platform's reputation from get-rich-quick tropes.
**S8. AGREE:** Total public transparency remains the platform's most vital feature.
**S9. AMEND:** Add a minimum trade count (e.g., 5 trades) so AIs cannot simply park cash in one safe asset to win "Steadiest climb." Overall: YES, run it.
